text:
alex: seeing widespread 502s from the EU inference LB starting ~09:12 UTC. app pods are Ready but LB health shows failed checks, traffic timed out

maria: looking into it, any recent infra changes in eu-west2?

alex: not that I'm aware of. attaching a VPC flow log line I grabbed:
`src=34.240.12.8 dst=10.10.4.12 sport=443 dport=31693 action=REJECT`

jin: REJECT on return path? that looks like a NACL deny. running `aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0abc123` to list rules now

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-0423 created and paged on-call

sam: I checked the public subnets NACLs — there's an explicit DENY tcp 1024-65535 for 0.0.0.0/0 with higher rule number than the allow. probably the culprit. :facepalm:

maria: that would block LB -> node ephemeral return traffic (health checks use ephemeral dst ports on nodes). makes sense why kube probes and LB fail but pods themselves look healthy locally

priya: who merged that NACL change? searching Terraform history and PRs now

alex: tcpdump on node while triggering LB check: `tcpdump -n -i eth0 'tcp and dst port 31693'` shows SYNs arriving from LB IPs but no SYN-ACK going back

jin: ok I'm going to patch the NACL to explicitly allow ephemeral ports 1024-65535 for TCP in both directions for the public subnets and re-apply. doing `terraform apply` now

sre-bot: terraform plan OK by jin for aws_nacl.public_subnet_rules

maria: after the apply I'm seeing LB health checks transition to healthy (3/3) within a minute

sam: root cause: a hardening attempt introduced a DENY that shadowed broader allows. follow-ups: add a pre-merge linter that rejects NACL rules with wide outbound denies on public subnets, and update runbook to check ephemeral ranges

priya: filing RFC to standardize ephemeral port policy for LB/node traffic and putting a guard in the infra repo. also creating a Jira to track the linter work

alex: re-checking autoscaling nodes and pod restarts — nothing else impacted. marking incident resolved after 18m

sre-bot: INC-2026-0423 resolved (duration 18m)

sam: postmortem notes: 1) NACL rule priorities confusing, DENY wins, 2) VPC flow logs + quick tcpdump are fast diagnostics, 3) add tests that simulate LB->node health check traffic in CI

maria: adding short blameless postmortem doc and linking PRs

alex: thanks everyone for the quick triage :thumbsup:
